summary: Slack OAuth is self-serve for private installs: create a Slack app, add your HTTPS redirect URI, request only the scopes you need, and install it. The catch is that Marketplace approval adds scope restrictions and a long manual review.
difficultyReason: Private installs are quick, but Slack Marketplace approval can take weeks and rejects restricted scopes or apps that are not production-ready.

timeToFirstLogin.text: About 15–30 minutes, but this is only an estimate.

timeToProduction.text: If you want Slack Marketplace approval, plan on up to 10 business days for preliminary feedback and up to 10 weeks for the functional review on new submissions.
timeToProduction.quote: up to 10 weeks for new submissions

costs.quote: We currently provide the Developer Services at no charge.

costs.text: Slack's Free plan is $0 and allows up to 10 apps.

requirements.text: You need a Slack workspace with privileges to install apps.
requirements.quote: A Slack workspace with privileges to install apps.

requirements.text: Your redirect URI must be HTTPS.
If you want Slack Marketplace review, your app must be installed on 10 or more active workspaces.
requirements.quote: installed on 10 or more active workspaces

reviewTriggers.text: Submitting the app to the Slack Marketplace triggers manual review.
reviewTriggers.quote: If you don't submit your app, we won't display it there

reviewTriggers.text: Changing approved scopes or adding new features later requires review again.
reviewTriggers.quote: you'll need your app to be reviewed again.

reviewTriggers.text: Slack flags restricted or broad scopes for Marketplace review, including identity.*, workflow.steps:execute, read, post, client, admin.*, search:read, and triggers:*.
reviewTriggers.quote: identity.*, workflow.steps:execute, read, post, client, admin.*, search:read, triggers:*

steps.title: Choose private install or Marketplace
steps.detail: If you only need a direct authorization URL, skip Marketplace. If you want Slack to list the app, plan for review.
steps.quote: If you don't submit your app, we won't display it there

steps.title: Create a Slack app
steps.detail: Open Slack App Management, click Create a Slack app, choose From Scratch, and pick the workspace where you will build and test.
steps.quote: Choose From Scratch and give your app a name and workspace to live on.

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.detail: Paste the exact HTTPS redirect URL into OAuth & Permissions and save it.

steps.title: Add the minimum scopes
steps.detail: Use only the bot scopes your app needs, and add user scopes only if your app must act on behalf of a user.
steps.quote: The `scope` list requests scopes for your app's bot user.

steps.title: Install and verify OAuth
steps.detail: Generate the authorization URL, install the app in a workspace you control, and confirm Slack returns a code to your redirect URI.
steps.quote: Redirecting a user to Slack can be done with a single link.

steps.title: Slack Marketplace review
steps.detail: If you want public distribution, submit the app, answer reviewer feedback, and resubmit until it is approved.
steps.quote: up to 10 weeks for new submissions

steps.title: Publish and keep scopes in sync
steps.detail: After approval, publish when ready. If scopes or redirect URIs change, update the live app and resubmit.
steps.quote: you'll need your app to be reviewed again.

blockers.problem: You want Marketplace approval but have not reached 10 active workspaces.
blockers.whatToDo: Get the app installed and tested on 10 or more active workspaces before submitting.
blockers.quote: installed on 10 or more active workspaces

blockers.problem: You request restricted or broad scopes for a Marketplace app.
blockers.whatToDo: Trim the scope list to the minimum and avoid restricted scopes before submitting again.
blockers.quote: identity.*, workflow.steps:execute, read, post, client, admin.*, search:read, triggers:*

blockers.problem: Your app needs bulk channel-history reads and is not Marketplace-approved.
blockers.whatToDo: Expect tighter limits on conversations.history and conversations.replies, or redesign around safer APIs.
blockers.quote: will be limited to 1 request per minute

blockers.problem: You are trying to use the old classic app model.
blockers.whatToDo: Use the v2 OAuth flow for a Slack app instead.
blockers.quote: You won't be able to create new classic apps

agentDrafts.title: App description
agentDrafts.text: Connect your Slack workspace so the AI agent can read the user-approved context, answer in Slack, and carry out approved actions.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need chat:write
agentDrafts.text: Needed so the agent can send approved replies, summaries, and status updates back into Slack.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need conversation history scopes
agentDrafts.text: Needed so the agent can read the recent Slack context it was explicitly allowed to access before it answers.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need read scopes for conversations
agentDrafts.text: Needed to list available channels and direct messages so the user can choose where the agent should work.

agentDrafts.title: Why we need users:read
agentDrafts.text: Needed to resolve user names and mentions so the agent can attribute messages correctly.

openQuestions: I did not confirm a separate business-verification step for ordinary Slack OAuth apps.
I did not find a fixed Slack test-user cap for private installs beyond the workspace app limits and Marketplace requirements.
Exact scopes depend on what your agent does, so I left the scope list generic.
